A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REVISE/EAGER research. All main-text and appendix pages were readable, including equations, algorithms, figures, and tables; relocated material could be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original REVISE benchmark evaluations, reinforcement fine-tuning results, and ablations, including the results in Table 6 and supplementary Tables 9–12.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark evaluations and reinforcement fine-tuning results in Tables 1–4, alongside empirical ablations and additional benchmark results in the appendix.

M1.justification: The written response/reward specification changes: v1 requires a summary with the final answer and scores z_tau; v2 emits the answer without a new summary and scores the last committed z_(tau-1). The selector, state fields, and GRPO remain intact. The explicit think trace was already depicted in v1 Figure 3, so it is not an entirely new component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate VideoEspresso, NExT-QA, EgoSchema, Video-MME, and LVBench. The latter two already appear in v1 Table 12. Open-ended generation is proposed only as future work in v2, not evaluated.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators, including VideoAgent, VideoTree, LVNet, LLoVi, Adaptive Keyframes, and MDP3. Corrected LVNet and LongVA-DPO citations do not change comparator membership; newly discussed frame-selection methods are not added to the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Table 10 changes the caption-analysis backbone heading from GPT-5.1 to GPT-4o. This revises the reported experimental setting, although neither PDF establishes that the experiment was rerun. Splits, metrics, interaction budgets, sampling settings, and training hyperparameters otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The tested ablation factors and analytical findings are retained: state carryover, structured fields, turns and frames, captions, summary drift, and reward sensitivity. v1 Tables 2 and 5 become v2 Tables 8 and 7, and Figure 4 moves to the appendix. The Table 10 backbone relabeling adds no ablation condition or analytical finding.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point estimates and error-category ranges. Neither adds empirical repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical scores and plotted trends remain unchanged after matching relocated material. However, Table 10 reattributes its result block from GPT-5.1 to GPT-4o, including 74.1% for frames-only REVISE and 75.4% with captions. This changes the model-specific results being reported, without demonstrating any same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: Section 3 revises the frame-set recurrence from S_t = S_(t-1) union F_(t+1) to S_(t+1) = S_t union F_(t+1). Equation (3.13) changes summary conditioning from z_tau to z_(tau-1). These are limited formal corrections; the GRPO equations and appendix RL derivations are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same central claims about sparse multi-round VQA, persistent summary state, EAGER, and accuracy/efficiency benefits in plug-and-play and reinforcement fine-tuning settings. No new principal contribution or stronger performance claim is introduced.

C2.justification: The conclusion adds whole-frame granularity as a limitation for fine-grained localization, with spatial cropping, stronger vision encoders, and open-ended generation suggested as future directions. Existing backbone-dependence and interaction-latency limitations and interpretations of the experiments remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page pointer in the abstract and clarifies output tags and transient versus persisted reasoning. Hardware, the 8,000 distilled conversations, and training hyperparameters are retained. The supplied PDFs do not establish what code or data the project page provides.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a substantial adaptive-frame-selection survey spanning training-free, learned, RL-based, and iterative-agent approaches, explicitly positioning REVISE's persistent state and EAGER against them. It also repairs the LVNet source mismatch and replaces the unrelated video-generation reference previously attached to LongVA-DPO.

P1.justification: v2 condenses repetitive introductory paragraphs, rewrites the response-protocol explanation, expands related work and limitations, and adds acknowledgements. Appendix subsections organize the relocated ablations. These are localized revisions within a largely retained narrative structure.

P2.justification: Two ablation tables and Figure 4 move from the main text to the appendix, with Figure 4 enlarged. Figure 3 updates protocol labels and its caption; its summary box changes from P/O/H/U/R to Answer. Other displays are mainly renumbered or reflowed, with no new figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v2 improves research context through the focused frame-selection survey, repairs source attribution, clarifies the terminal-summary protocol, and states an additional applicability limitation. These are useful but limited gains; empirical evidence is not strengthened. The unexplained GPT-5.1-to-GPT-4o reassignment in Table 10 and misleading Answer label in Figure 3 temper the improvement.
